transport: Bluetooth 4.0 / BLE on the phone side, RS-485 on the controller side. The GATT service and characteristic UUIDs, and whether Modbus frames pass through transparently, are not documented in any source found.
sharedMapEvidence: Like the eBox-WIFI-01 this is a transport adapter, not a map — but unlike it, nothing found describes the wire format. EPEVER publishes a datasheet and a user manual, both of which describe the phone app, not the BLE protocol. No reverse-engineering work was found. Filed as no-comms in the sense that matters here: there is no protocol Cabin Hub could implement against today. Do not confuse this wi
gotchas: Occupies the controller's only RS-485 port, same as the WiFi box.

The Pi 5's onboard BLE could in principle reach it (docs/DEVICES.md already notes the Pi covers Victron BLE with no extra hardware), so the hardware cost is zero — the blocker is entirely that no protocol is published.
The XTRA-N G3 BLE models have Bluetooth built in and do not need this adapter at all. Their BLE protocol is equally undocumented.
